Respondents Date of institution : 16.06.2023 Nature of the Case : Seeking  Compensation/Award Date of commencement of : 29.06.2024 Recording of evidence Date of Judgment : 06.09.2023 pronounced  JUDGMENT The petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

02. The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that:
on 31.05.2023 at about 1.00 p.m.(noon) when he was proceeding as pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KR-7901, on Shamanna Garden-Vijayanagar Pipe Line road, at that time rider of the said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the footpath edge at Shamanna Garden bridge,
caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the rider of the motor cycle shifted him to the Re-life hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident and spent huge amount towards medicine and conveyance.

It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to the accident,
he is unable to work and as such, he has sustained loss of earnings and he is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.

It is further stated in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KR- 7901, and as such, the 1st respondent being the owner, 2nd respondent being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Sabanna vs Jafar Sadiq on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193264566/
2 03.
On service of summons, 2nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the 1 st respondent remained absent, hence he was placed exparte.
04. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-02-KR-7901 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further stated that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective riding license at the time of the accident and also denied the manner of accident, age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Denied the negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
Among other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

05. On the above pleadings, my predecessor has framed issues as follows:
1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 31.05.2023 at about 1.00 p.m.(noon) when he was proceeding as pillion in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-KR- 7901, on Shamanna Garden-vijayanagar Pipe Line road, at that time rider of the said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the footpath edge at Shamanna Garden bridge, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries as alleged by him?
2) Whether the petitioner entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 ) What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and produced documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to P14.

Also got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and they got marked documents at Ex.P14 to 18 and closed their side of evidence.
07.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and he got marked two documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.

Also one witness is examined as RW.2 and he got marked Ex.R3 documents.
08.
Heard arguments.

10. Issue No.1:- The claim of the petitioner is that on 31.05.2023 at about 1.00 p.m.(noon) when he was proceeding as pillion in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 02-KR-7901, on Shamanna Garden-vijayanagar Pipe Line road, at that time rider of the said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the footpath edge at Shamanna Garden bridge, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove the issue examined himself as PW.1 by filing affidavit as his examination in chief and produced IFR, Complaint, Mahazar, Sketch, 133 notice & reply IMV report, wound certificate and Charge Sheet which were marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
11.

On the other hand it is the contention of the Respondent No.2 that alleged motorcycle is not involved in the accident, the petitioner and owner of the motorcycle colluded with police officials,
registered the false complaint and created the other document.

In support of their contention Respondent No.2 has examined the MRO of the Re-life Hospital, Bengaluru, as Rw1 and got marked Ex.R1 and 2 which are the authorization letter to adduce evidence and certified copy of the MLC extract.

It is the specific contention of the respondent No.2 that MLC was created by the hospital colluding with the petitioner and also put the suggestion in this regard, but RW1 has denied the said suggestion.

He admits that, In original MLC Register, front and back side of the pages mentioned as July month, and in the middle of the page mentioned as 31.05.2023, but the said Rw1 is not the author of the said document, he is only authorized for production of the said document.
In support of the version of the Respondent No.2, they have not produced other cogent oral and documentary evidence.
RW.2 who is the legal manager of the Respondent No.2 company has deposed that their company has not conducted separate enquiry through the private investigation agencies.

This makes it clear that except the entry in the MLC register there is no supportive document and also Rw1 is not the author of the said register, therefore without supportive document and evidence, the contention of the Respondent not believable.
12. The first information was given by the Honnamma who is the wife of the injured person on 02.06.2023 and the accident was occurred on 31.05.2023 after 2 days delay.
On the basis of the information the police attached to the Magadi Road Traffic PS, registered FIR for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
The petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 31.05.2023 soon after the accident.

13. The PW.3 produced case sheet and X-rays marked as Ex.P17 and Ex.P18 goes to show that on 31.05.2023 at about 3.30 p.m. the petitioner was admitted to the hospital and the history mentioned in the MLC register is the road traffic accident petitioner was pillion rider near Gowripalya on 31.05.2023 at about 1:00 PM.
On the same day, the hospital authority issued intimation to the police.
Hence, it is the duty of the IO or anybody on his behalf to visit the hospital and to receive the information regarding the alleged accident.
Since the police have not rushed to the hospital, the first informant being the wife of the injured in the said accident went to the police station on 02.06.2023 and lodged first information.
The petitioner was admitted in the hospital and he was unable to given first information and police have not received the information from him in the hospital.
Hence, the petitioner unable to give first information on the date of accident.
The first informant in her information has stated that she engaged in the hospital to look after the petitioner.

The first priority Sabanna vs Jafar Sadiq on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193264566/
4 is to look after the petitioner.

The wound certificate discloses that the injury caused to the petitioner is severe, hence all the family members including the first informant were busy in the hospital and hence they have not given first information to the police on the date of accident.
Hence there was delay of 2 days that cannot be doubted.
14. The IMV report marked as Ex.P7 discloses that the accident was not due to mechanical defect of the vehicles.

The respondent has not obtained any favourable answer from the mouth of PW.1 to prove that there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KR-7901 vehicle and there is fault on the part of the petitioner.
The rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02- KR-7901 rode his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the footpath edge.

Hence, there is a negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KR-7901.
15.

Ex.P9 is the charge sheet wherein the I.O after investigation filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle since during the time of investigation he found that there was negligence on part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
There is no evidence before this tribunal that the Investigation Officer in order to help the petitioner filed the false charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.

The documents placed before the tribunal coupled with oral evidence establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.KA-02-KR-7901 and petitioner sustained injuries in the said accident.

Hence I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Reg No. KA-02-KR-7901.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
But the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his avocation and income.
Hence, in the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2023.
Considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- per month as per the table of the KASLA.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
In order to prove his contention petitioner has examined the doctor who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital as PW.2 who assessed the disability of the petitioner.
He deposed that, petitioners has sustained open fracture of tibia and fibula of left leg.
Petitioner has undergone internal fixation to tibia left leg.
Doctor has assessed 28% disability to the left lower limb and 14% as whole body disability.

sentences.text: While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.2 is not a treated doctor.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 10% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 32 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 31.05.2023.
However, by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P11 Adhaar card as 01.01.1990, the petitioner was aged 33 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 33 is 16 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,07,200/-(Rs.16,000x12x10x16/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

18. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
Due to the injuries sustained, the petitioner took treatment at Re-life hospital.

Further Ex.P8 Wound certificate issued by the said hospital discloses that the petitioner has sustained open wound with fracture of left tibia and fibula short left and the doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 reveals that petitioner was admitted as inpatient at Re-life Hospital, Bengaluru, from 31.05.2023 to 06.06.2023 and took treatment.
The petitioner was aged about 33 years.
In that age he suffered a lot and also suffering from pain due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence by considering the age, the nature of injuries and the period of inpatient in the hospital the petitioner is entitled for Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
19. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced prescriptions at Ex.P12 and medical bills at Ex.P13 for Rs.2,34,984/-.
On perusal of the said bills, it is clear that petitioner has taken treatment for the accidental injuries.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,34,984/- under this head.

20. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 7 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Sabanna vs Jafar Sadiq on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193264566/
6
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.10,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital
, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.48,000/- (16,000X3) under this head.

22. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.
This court has considered disability to the extent of 10% to whole body.
Considering all these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- on this head.
23. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
The doctor stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
Petitioner has to undergo surgery, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

23. Thus in all, the petitioner entitled for the compensation as here under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount  No. Compensation 1. Loss of future earnings due Rs. 3,07,200/-
to disability 2. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 50,000/-

3 . Medical expenses Rs. 2,34,984/-
4. Conveyance, food and Rs. 10,000/-
 nourishment, attendant  charges and other incidental  expenses.

5. Loss of income during laid Rs.
 up period 48,000/-

7 6. Loss of amenities in life/Life Rs. 20,000/-
comforts and expectancy of life 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs 7,00,184/-

. 
In total, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,00,184/- (Seven Lakhs one hundred and eighty four only).
24.
Interest:
The petitioner is claiming interest @ 9% p.a. on the compensation amount.

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding medical expenses) is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-02-KR-7901.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,00,184/-(Rupees Seven lakhs one hundred and eighty four only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on Rs.6,70,184/-(excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realisation.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 60% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by Sabanna vs Jafar Sadiq on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193264566/
8 way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 40% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 2 years.
